Shown while the field is focused and the local browsing history (plus any open tab) has no HTTP(S) destination to offer yet. Not a loading state and not a network search. No placeholders.

ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.role: status or explanatory text — address suggestions
ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.note: Shown while the field holds input the browser will not open: a blocked scheme (javascript:, data:, about:, an unknown scheme) or a file: URL. It states the rule before Enter, so the refusal is not a surprise. No placeholders.

ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_searc.role: first row — address suggestions, search intent
ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_searc.note: The first, highlighted row when the typed text is a search rather than a URL. It names the destination explicitly (DuckDuckGo) so the user knows where Enter will send the query. Placeholders: query = the user’s typed text, already trimmed.

ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.role: secondary line of an address suggestion row
ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.note: Marks a suggestion that comes from a tab this browser still has open, rather than from the persistent history. It is a source marker, not an action: committing the row navigates the CURRENT tab to that URL, it does not switch tabs. Placeholders: title = the page title.

ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.role: secondary line of an address suggestion row
ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.note: The same source marker as address_suggestion_open_tab when the open tab has no page title yet. Committing the row navigates the current tab, not a tab switch. No placeholders.

ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.role: accessible control/region name — address suggestions list
ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.note: Names the suggestion list when EVERY row comes from the persistent local history. It must never sit over a web-search row or an open-tab row: use address_suggestions_label_mixed for those. Keep the label short, around the English footprint. No placeholders.

ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.role: accessible control/region name — address suggestions list
ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.note: Names the suggestion list when it contains anything other than persistent history — the DuckDuckGo search row, open-tab rows, or the empty state. It is deliberately neutral: it claims nothing about where the rows came from. Keep it short, around the English footprint. No placeholders.
Shown when browsing history exists but the typed prefix and titles match nothing. Distinct from the no-history message and from the unavailable message. No placeholders.

ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.role: status or explanatory text — address suggestions
ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.tone: plain, restrained; the field still works
ui.browser.browser_url_bar.address_sugge.note: Shown when the local history read failed. It states the degradation and nothing more: typing and Enter still navigate normally, and no retry control is offered. No placeholders.

ui.browser.browser_passkey_notice.passke.role: accessible region name — passkey notice strip
ui.browser.browser_passkey_notice.passke.tone: Plain explanatory language; preserve confidence and safety meaning
ui.browser.browser_passkey_notice.passke.note: Accessible name of the strip that tells the user a page asked for a passkey. Length: keep compact, around the English footprint.

ui.browser.browser_passkey_notice.messag.tone: Plain explanatory language; preserve confidence and safety meaning
ui.browser.browser_passkey_notice.messag.note: Names who asked for a passkey. {who} is agent (tab driven by an agent), agentFrame (an embedded frame in an agent-driven tab), userFrame (an embedded frame on the user's page) or other (the page itself); {site} is a host name, never translate it. Say the request MAY still be waiting: the page's request was neither refused nor answered. Do not say it failed. 'Agent' follows the glossary term for AI agent.

ui.browser.browser_passkey_notice.explan.tone: Plain explanatory language; preserve confidence and safety meaning
ui.browser.browser_passkey_notice.explan.note: States plainly that passkeys do not work in this browser yet, that Touch ID passkeys are planned (a plan, not a promise or date), and to use the system browser meanwhile. Do not name unsupported hardware and do not give dates.

ui.browser.browser_passkey_notice.open_i.tone: Plain explanatory language; preserve confidence and safety meaning
ui.browser.browser_passkey_notice.open_i.note: Opens the current page in the user's default web browser. Keep compact, around the English footprint.

ui.browser.browser_passkey_notice.dismis.role: accessible control name — passkey notice strip
ui.browser.browser_passkey_notice.dismis.tone: Plain explanatory language; preserve confidence and safety meaning
ui.browser.browser_passkey_notice.dismis.note: Dismisses the passkey notice. Keep compact, around the English footprint.

ui.browser.use_browser_chrome.passkey_op.tone: Plain explanatory language; preserve confidence and safety meaning
ui.browser.use_browser_chrome.passkey_op.note: Shown when handing the page to the system browser was refused or failed. {reason} is the app's own reason sentence, already in English or the user's language; keep it as the last sentence.
